A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same H-CAST framework despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including content moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original hierarchical classification experiments, architecture and loss ablations, and qualitative and quantitative segmentation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds benchmark comparisons, iNaturalist results, visual-grounding analyses and loss ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions use SEEDS superpixels, CAST graph pooling, fine-to-coarse classification heads and cross-entropy combined with Tree-path KL divergence. Equations (1)–(3) remain equivalent; renaming spatial consistency to visual consistency and disclosing additional settings do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds iNaturalist2021-Mini with order, family and name labels, extending biological taxonomy coverage within the existing classification task. BREEDS, CUB, Aircraft and ImageNet-S remain. iNaturalist2018 was already evaluated in v1 Figure 1, so its expanded comparison in v2 is not a newly introduced dataset.

E2.justification: v2 adds FGN, HRN, TransHP and HiE to benchmark comparisons, plus zero-shot CLIP and BIOCLIP evaluations. Table 10 also compares against Guided and HiMulConE using scores attributed to TransHP. ViT-Single, CAST-Single and ViT-Hier remain under the names Flat-ViT, Flat-CAST and Hier-ViT.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include zero-shot foundation-model comparisons, thresholded Grad-CAM overlap/correlation measurements, HRN batch-size comparisons and the selected three-level iNat21-Mini hierarchy. v2 specifies 300 epochs for the added TransHP comparator. Retained H-CAST settings largely match, although the reported CUB training count changes from 5,944 to 5,994; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds KL-versus-BCE/flat-consistency ablations, Living-17 loss ablations, quantitative Grad-CAM alignment analysis, nearest-neighbor feature analysis, H-CAST attention maps and HRN batch-size sensitivity results. These substantially expand tests of the proposed mechanism and design choices. The original direction ablation, two-loss Aircraft ablation and segmentation comparison are retained.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly acknowledges insufficient runs for error bars in its checklist. v2 removes that disclosure and introduces plus/minus values for overlap and correlation scores in Table 3, without identifying their statistical meaning. Main benchmark results still lack uncertainty estimates, and no increase in run counts is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive comparator and analysis results, including H-CAST FPA of 64.92 on iNat21-Mini. Original H-CAST benchmark scores and segmentation mIoUs remain unchanged, but some baseline values change: Living-17 CAST-Single/Flat-CAST FPA becomes 78.82 instead of 79.82. The original iNat2018 correctness breakdown disappears, while added batch-8 HRN rows lead FPA on CUB and Aircraft under their stated settings.

T1.justification: The hierarchy definitions and method equations remain equivalent. Appendix A newly defines thresholded Grad-CAM masks, their overlap count and correlation restricted to overlapping pixels in Equations (4)–(6). This is a limited addition of mathematical definitions for analysis; no theoretical guarantees or proofs are added.

C1.justification: H-CAST, Tree-path KL loss and improved hierarchical accuracy/consistency remain the central contributions. v2 adds an explicit headline claim of outperforming zero-shot CLIP and state-of-the-art methods, while revising the introduction's claimed FPA improvement from 17–25 percentage points to 3–10 points.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of CLIP's coarse-category failures, class-relevant versus superficial feature learning, loss-related accuracy/consistency tradeoffs and HRN's batch-size sensitivity. It removes v1 Appendix A.3's explicit superpixel-dependence limitation and the discussion of the llama segmentation failure, although that failure image remains.

D1.justification: v2 provides a code-access link instead of a future-release promise and newly specifies alpha = 0.5, the DeiT training framework, comparator configurations and iNaturalist training details. Most original hyperparameters remain unchanged. Conversely, v1's disclosure of four 40GB NVIDIA A40 GPUs disappears with the checklist.

R1.justification: v2 replaces the label-embedding/loss/architecture survey with positioning around single-level versus full-taxonomy prediction and external semantic versus internal visual consistency. It substantially expands discussion of foundation models, TransHP, HiE and hierarchical semantic segmentation, while removing much of the older embedding and pre-deep-learning coverage.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. BREEDS becomes the central comparison, Aircraft/CUB results move to Appendix E.5, a Summary section is added, and the appendices are reorganized into A–E. The NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: v2 adds a positioning diagram, Grad-CAM and CLIP displays, nearest-neighbor comparisons and attention visualizations; it also redraws the architecture diagram and reorganizes segmentation examples. Benchmark tables gain comparator/configuration columns, Aircraft/CUB tables move to the appendix, and the original ablation tables are transposed and combined into Table 2.

improvement.justification: v1's main comparative evidence relied largely on internally constructed ViT/CAST baselines. v2 substantially strengthens validation through published competitors, large-scale three-level evaluation and targeted grounding/loss analyses. Important qualifications remain: Tables 11–12 contain superiority captions despite HRN configurations achieving higher FPA, and the explicit superpixel limitation is removed. These weaknesses temper the claims but do not outweigh the substantially stronger comparative and diagnostic evidence.
